subject: Pilot data TTL and PII carveout — next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot data TTL and PII carveout — next steps

Tom / Anna,

Great speaking with you today — thanks for the demo and for walking through the NovaMed pilot goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

• Scope: 1-week pilot, 2 production-like endpoints (triage chat + batch extraction).
• Data handling ask you raised: zero retention for any PII tokens, shortened KV/telemetry window for debug purposes, and residency in us-east-1.
• Redwood proposal: two options (attached):
  - Ephemeral mode (PII redaction + no persistent KV writes) — near zero retention for user inputs; logs only stored transiently for debugging for up to 6 hours.
  - Short-TTL mode: redacted PII retained 0 hours, non-PII KV cache TTL 7 days; debug logs 30 days with access controls.

I'd like to loop in Aditya (security) and Marissa (solutions) to validate feasibility and highlight any additional evidence you’ll need for procurement. Action items: 
1) Aditya to confirm technical feasibility and evidence (SOC 2, config controls).
2) NovaMed to confirm preferred option (Ephemeral vs Short-TTL) and any legal/litigation holds to be aware of.
3) If Ephemeral preferred, legal and deployment ops will need explicit acceptance of feature tradeoffs (e.g., limited debugging window).

Attached: redwood_data_retention_options.pdf (summarizes controls + SLO tradeoffs).

Thanks — I’ll follow up after Aditya weighs in.

— Laura

From: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@novamed.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot data TTL and PII carveout — next steps

Laura — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from our side after discussing with Security and Legal: 

1) Our priority is strict PII non-retention. If you can guarantee 0 retention for PII (no writes to persistent logs or KV), that would be ideal. We understand ephemeral mode may limit debugging — that's acceptable for the pilot but we need a clear escalation path.
2) For non-PII KV/cache (e.g., conversation context), legal is pushing for a 24h TTL rather than 7 days for the initial pilot. We can revisit longer TTLs after a successful pilot.
3) Residency: us-east-1 required; any cross-region backups must be disabled.

Can you confirm if Ephemeral + 24h KV for non-PII is feasible? If so, please send the security questionnaire back once you confirm configuration so we can move procurement forward.

— Tom

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot data TTL and PII carveout — next steps

Tom / Laura / Marissa — thanks. Short answers up front: feasible with guardrails. Details below: 

1) Ephemeral PII (0 retention): We can configure request-level redaction and prevent write-to-disk for any fields flagged as PII in the ingestion pipeline. That achieves zero persistent retention. Runtime traces will be kept in memory for the request lifecycle only. For auditing, we can surface request hashes (no PII) and delivery metrics.

2) KV TTL 24h (non-PII): We can enforce a 24-hour TTL on the application-level KV cache for the pilot. Important: aggressive TTL can increase token counts (cold-start context) which affects latency/cost; we’ll include recommendations in the MAP.

3) Residency and backups: We will deploy the pilot in us-east-1 and can disable cross-region backups. Note: platform-managed snapshots are optional — we will disable them for this deal and document it in the deployment runbook.

4) Evidence: We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary, config screenshots (RBAC, KMS key bindings), and an audit log extract for feature flags once the pilot cluster is provisioned. Expect initial artifacts within 3 business days after contract signature.

5) Operational caveat: Ephemeral + no persistent logs reduces our ability to debug intermittent telemetry issues. Suggest we add a short-term emergency-debug path: on-call escalation that can enable ephemeral debugging for a targeted window (audit logged and customer-approved). This is a standard tradeoff.

Next steps: 
• Marissa to prepare MAP and draft configuration appendix specifying PII redaction, 24h KV TTL, and backup settings.
• Laura to capture acceptance in SOW/contract appendix.
• Tom to return signed security questionnaire (attached) and confirm DocuSign path when ready.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
